articles.title: Government may allow fees on UPI payment above Rs 2,000
articles.description: The government may allow a small charge on UPI payments exceeding two thousand rupees. This levy would apply to transactions made to businesses and not individuals.  Official estimates suggest this change will impact only five percent of all UPI transactions.  Most daily purchases like groceries and taxi fares will remain unaffected by this potential fee.  Industry experts anticipate a possible ceiling on the absolute amount charged for these transactions.

articles.title: 2 ISI-backed terror modules busted: Pistols, petrol bombs seized, 9 arrested
articles.description: Punjab Police apprehended nine individuals, including four juveniles, in two ISI-backed terror modules.  Authorities recovered illegal firearms, petrol bombs, and a stolen motorcycle from the arrested suspects.  The accused were reportedly recruiting local youth for terror activities and conducting surveillance.  These individuals acted at the behest of handlers from the Inter-Services Intelligence agency.  The police operation successfully dismantled these cross-border terror networks.

articles.title: BSE Sensex, NSE Nifty50 eye RBI MPC decision after ending four-day winning streak
articles.full_text: Oil prices recovered modestly in early trade after suffering steep losses in the previous session, as investors continued to assess developments in West Asia and their potential impact on global crude supplies. Brent crude futures rose 31 cents, or 0.39%, to $79.67 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 11 cents, or 0.15%, to $75.88 a barrel. The rebound came after oil prices fell on Tuesday following comments from Qatar that mediators were making progress in efforts to end the conflict in the region. The prospect of easing geopolitical tensions reduced concerns over possible supply disruptions, dragging crude prices lower. However, uncertainty remained after Tehran rejected US President Donald Trump's claim that talks were already underway. Market participants continue to monitor diplomatic developments closely, with any breakthrough or escalation likely to influence crude prices and, in turn, investor sentiment across global financial markets. Market experts attributed the recent volatility primarily to the introduction of the Closing Auction Session rather than any deterioration in the broader economic outlook. According to Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth, benchmark indices experienced a phase of recalibration after Monday's auction lifted the closing prices of several heavyweight stocks. Tuesday's session saw prices move back towards levels established during continuous trading, resulting in increased volatility. Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments said the combination of weekly expiry and the revised F&O closing price mechanism temporarily distorted market trends. Vikram Kasat of PL Capital noted that investors also used the session to book profits in large-cap financial and IT stocks after the previous day's rally. Analysts broadly agreed that the fluctuations reflected evolving market mechanics and investor positioning rather than structural weaknesses, with healthy auction volumes indicating continued institutional participation. Indian benchmark equity indices ended lower after snapping a four-session winning streak, with investors navigating heightened volatility following the rollout of the Closing Auction Session (CAS) for stocks with futures and options contracts. BSE Sensex fell 210.08 points to settle at 78,428.95, while NSE Nifty declined 159.40 points to close at 24,614.90. Markets had started the session on a mixed note but gradually lost momentum as investors booked profits in several large-cap stocks. Analysts said the adjustment was driven less by changes in fundamentals and more by the market adapting to the new auction-based closing price discovery system. The new mechanism, introduced to improve transparency and robustness in determining closing prices, led to significant shifts in benchmark-heavy stocks. Despite the decline in headline indices, broader market performance remained mixed, reflecting selective buying in pockets of the market.
